topic.subject: science
topic.title: Pollution of air and water
topic.scope: air pollutants, smog, acid rain, greenhouse effect and global warming, water pollution, potable water, Ganga action plan

misconceptions.statement: Air pollution only happens outdoors in big cities.
misconceptions.why: Students associate pollution with visible smoke from factories and cars seen in urban environments.
misconceptions.fix: Air pollution also occurs indoors due to cooking fuels, incense sticks, and poor ventilation.

probe.question: Can the air inside a house be polluted if no one is smoking?
probe.wrong_answer: No, because pollution only comes from cars and factories outside.

misconceptions.statement: Smog is just a thick cloud of natural fog.
misconceptions.why: The word 'smog' sounds like 'fog' and they look visually similar to the naked eye.
misconceptions.fix: Smog is a mixture of smoke and fog, where smoke contains harmful pollutants like particulates.

probe.question: Is smog harmful to breathe in?
probe.wrong_answer: No, it is just natural fog that makes it hard to see.

misconceptions.statement: Clear, sparkling water is always safe to drink.
misconceptions.why: Students equate visual clarity with purity, ignoring invisible pathogens or dissolved chemicals.
misconceptions.fix: Water can look clear but still contain harmful bacteria, viruses, or toxic dissolved chemicals.

probe.question: If water from a river looks crystal clear, can we drink it directly?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, because clear water is clean and free from pollution.

misconceptions.statement: Boiling water removes all types of pollution.
misconceptions.why: Students learn that boiling kills germs and overgeneralize this to all pollutants like heavy metals.
misconceptions.fix: Boiling kills microorganisms but does not remove dissolved chemical pollutants like lead or pesticides.

probe.question: Does boiling water remove chemical pesticides?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, boiling cleans the water of all harmful things.

misconceptions.statement: The greenhouse effect is inherently bad for the Earth.
misconceptions.why: The term is almost always discussed in the context of global warming and environmental damage.
misconceptions.fix: The natural greenhouse effect is essential to keep the Earth warm enough to support life.

probe.question: Would the Earth be better off without any greenhouse gases?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, because then there would be no global warming.

misconceptions.statement: Global warming is caused by a hole in the ozone layer.
misconceptions.why: Students often conflate two major environmental issues discussed in the same curriculum units.
misconceptions.fix: Global warming is caused by the trapping of heat by greenhouse gases, while the ozone hole is a separate issue related to UV radiation.

probe.question: What is the main cause of the Earth getting warmer?
probe.wrong_answer: The hole in the ozone layer lets in too much heat.
